analysis.title: AI Adoption Tracker: October 2026: Adoption Rises to 24.6%
key_insights: AI adoption among US establishments rose 0.8pp to 24.6% in the Census Bureau's BTOS, and firms expect adoption of 28.6% within 6 months. Adoption is approaching 50% in the information, professional and finance sectors.

At the subsector level, computing/data/web hosting, securities/commodities/financial and publishing firms lead adoption. Over half of establishments with 250+ employees expect to be using AI within six months.
Equity analysts expect global semiconductor revenue to reach $872bn (annualized) by end-2026. 2026 gross profit forecast revisions since 2022Q3 for AI-exposed global public companies stand at $1.1tn.
AI-related hardware investment in the US national accounts is $613bn above its 2022 level (3-month annualized average), equal to 1.9% of GDP.

AI-related hardware shipments from Taiwan are 88% above September 2022 levels. South Korea tech exports rose $8.8bn to $56bn in September. GS expects $82bn in global AI-related net exports from AI exporters in October.

Labor market drag is visible in industries with established AI use cases (marketing, graphic design, customer service, some tech occupations). Average monthly job growth in AI-affected industries is -6k over the last 3 months.
Data-center-exposed construction employment is up 315k since 2022 relative to broader construction employment trends.

Across nonmanufacturing subsectors, 3-month averages show a statistically significant relationship between AI adoption and weaker job growth (t-stat -2.07) and higher unemployment (t-stat 4.20). Effects on other labor outcomes (hours, real earnings, job finding rate, layoff rate) are not significant.

Corporate layoffs attributed to AI affected 4.0k employees in the latest month, bringing the total since May 2023 to 207k. 23% of Russell 3000 companies that have reported Q3 results mentioned AI- and labor-related keywords on earnings calls.

Productivity gains are large where generative AI is deployed but economy-wide effects are modest. Academic studies imply a 23% average uplift (median 20%) and company anecdotes imply about 32% (median 30%).

Industries with higher AI adoption show a slight acceleration in productivity growth over the past year in official US data. GS finds no relationship between company-level AI exposure and margin growth.

Dun & Bradstreet (October 2026): 65% of businesses plan to raise AI spending but only 28% report broad or strong returns. Only 8% say their data is fully ready for AI at scale. Eastern Europe (31%), Asia Pacific (30%) and Western Europe (30%) report the highest ROI rates.

KPMG (September 2026): 62% of organizations are building or deploying AI agents, up from 53% last quarter. General workforce adoption of AI tools rose to 44% from 23% last quarter. McKinsey (August 2026): 40% of large organizations are scaling AI agents, up from 27%.
earnings_insights: 23% of Russell 3000 companies that have reported Q3 results so far mentioned AI- and labor-related keywords in their earnings calls (per GS Data Works).

risk_factors: Data readiness: only 8% of businesses report enterprise data as fully ready to support AI at scale (Dun & Bradstreet), a possible hurdle to future adoption and productivity returns.
Gap between spending and returns: 65% of businesses plan to increase AI spending but only 28% report broad or strong returns.
Labor displacement: employment drags persist in AI-exposed industries and a positive correlation between AI adoption and unemployment among younger workers continues.
Survey wording change: the Census Bureau's December 2025 question rewording caused a level shift in adoption data, which complicates comparison with earlier readings.

tension_points.bull_case: Productivity gains are large where generative AI is deployed (23% academic average, 32% company anecdotes), and industries with higher adoption show slightly faster productivity growth. Data-center-exposed construction employment is up 315k since 2022.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher AI adoption at the subsector level is associated with weaker job growth and higher unemployment. Job growth in AI-affected industries is -6k a month and tech's employment share is below its long-run trend.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Job growth in AI-affected industries stays negative while adoption keeps rising toward the 28.6% expected in six months, which would confirm the labor drag. The report does not state a specific invalidation level for the bull case.

theme_stances.evidence: higher adoption associated with weaker job growth and higher unemployment
